> **In short:** Zapier lets you connect your email, spreadsheet, and other apps so that when an email arrives, the information automatically fills into a spreadsheet without you lifting a finger. Here's how to set it up step by step.

# How to Automate Business Tasks with Zapier — Step by Step

The average small business owner spends two to three hours every week copying information from emails into spreadsheets — order details, inquiry forms, sign-up confirmations. It is the kind of work that adds up without adding value.

There is a simpler way. A tool called Zapier acts as a bridge between the apps your business already uses. When something happens in one app (an email arrives), Zapier automatically does something in another app (adds a row to your spreadsheet). This is a simple form of what the industry calls an **AI agent (a smart software program that performs tasks across your apps automatically, without you needing to do each step manually)**.

Below is a step-by-step walkthrough for building your first automation. You will need a free Zapier account and a Google account for Sheets.

## Step 1 — Sign up for Zapier and start a new Zap

Open your browser and go to **zapier.com**. Click the **Sign up** button in the top right corner. You can create an account with your email address or sign in with Google — the Google option is faster if you already use Gmail and Google Sheets.

Once you are logged in, you will land on your dashboard. Look for the large orange button on the left side that says **Create Zap**. Click it.

💬 *Copy this:* Visit **zapier.com** → click **Sign up** (top right) → sign in with Google for quickest setup.

You'll know it worked when you see the Zap editor screen, which has a section labeled **Trigger** on the left and an **Action** section on the right.

---

## Step 2 — Set your trigger app (the thing that starts the automation)

In the Zap editor, click the **Trigger** section. A search box will appear labeled **App event**. Type **Email** and select **Email by Zapier** from the results. This is Zapier's built-in email tool — it gives your Zap its own inbox address.

After selecting Email, a second field will appear labeled **Event**. Click it and choose **New Email**. This tells Zapier: "When a new email arrives in your Zapier inbox, run this automation."

You will now see a field for your **Zapier Inbox Email Address**. Copy this address — you will use it in a moment. At the top of the Zap editor, give your Zap a name by clicking the **Untitled Zap** text and typing something like "Email to Sheet".

💬 *Copy this:* **Trigger App:** Email by Zapier → **Event:** New Email → copy your Zapier inbox email address.

You'll know it worked when you see a field displaying your unique inbox address in the format `yourname-zapier@email.zapier.com`.

---

## Step 3 — Forward an email to your Zapier inbox

Now you need to test that Zapier can actually see your emails. Open your regular email account (Gmail, Outlook, or whatever you use for business). Find any email — it does not matter which one.

Look for the **Forward** option in your email toolbar. Paste your Zapier inbox address into the forward field and send it.

Go back to the Zapier tab. In the Zap editor, click the **Test trigger** button near the bottom of the trigger section. Zapier will reach out and pull in the email you just forwarded. You should see the email subject, sender, and body appear in a preview box.

💬 *Copy this:* In your email → Forward → paste `yourname-zapier@email.zapier.com` → send → click **Test trigger** in Zapier.

You'll know it worked when the preview on screen shows the exact email you forwarded — subject line, sender address, and body text all matching.

---

## Step 4 — Connect Google Sheets as your action app

Now click the **Action** section on the right side of the Zap editor. A search box will appear labeled **App**. Type **Google Sheets** and select it from the results.

A second field will appear labeled **Event**. Click it and choose **Create Spreadsheet Row**. This tells Zapier: "When a new email arrives, add a new row to this spreadsheet."

Zapier will ask you to connect your Google account if you have not done so already. Click **Sign in to Google Sheets**, grant the permissions, and return to the Zap editor.

Now you need to tell Zapier which spreadsheet and which sheet tab to use. In the **Spreadsheet** field, select your spreadsheet from the dropdown. In the **Worksheet** field, select the specific tab inside that spreadsheet (for example, "Sheet1").

Below that you will see a list of your spreadsheet's column headers. Click each one and map it to the corresponding part of the email — drag the **Subject** field into one column, **From** (sender) into another, and **Body Plain** into a third. This tells Zapier exactly where to put each piece of information.

💬 *Copy this:* **Action App:** Google Sheets → **Event:** Create Spreadsheet Row → connect Google account → select your spreadsheet and worksheet tab → map email fields to columns.

You'll know it worked when the column mapping screen shows a line from each email field (Subject, From, Body Plain) into your spreadsheet columns, with the dropdowns all showing green ticks.

---

## Step 5 — Test your automation end to end

With the mapping done, click the **Test** button at the bottom of the Action section. Zapier will run a live test — it will send the email you forwarded earlier straight into a new row in your Google Sheet.

Open your Google Sheet and check. You should see a brand new row at the top (or bottom, depending on your sheet settings) with the email subject in one column, the sender's address in another, and the body text in a third.

If the data looks correct, click the orange **Publish** button in the top right corner of the Zap editor. Your Zap is now live.

💬 *Copy this:* Click **Test** → open Google Sheet → verify row was created → click **Publish** (top right).

You'll know it worked when the Publish button turns gray and shows a green tick, and when a new row appears in your spreadsheet moments after you forward an email.

---

## Step 6 — Use your automation in the real world

Now that your Zap is live, you can start using it properly. Instead of manually copying data, you simply forward relevant emails to your Zapier inbox address whenever you receive an order, a sign-up, or an inquiry.

Create a rule in your email app to automatically forward certain emails. In Gmail, go to **Settings → See all settings → Filters → Create a new filter**. Set your conditions (for example, emails with "order" in the subject) and check the box **Forward it to** — paste your Zapier inbox address there.

This means every order email your business receives will automatically flow into your spreadsheet without you touching it.

💬 *Copy this:* Gmail → **Settings → See all settings → Filters → Create a new filter** → condition: subject contains "order" → **Forward it to:** `yourname-zapier@email.zapier.com` → Create filter.

You'll know it worked when emails matching your filter automatically appear as new rows in your spreadsheet within a minute or two of arriving in your inbox.

---

## Common mistakes

**Mistake 1: Sending test emails to the wrong address**
It is easy to forget which inbox belongs to which Zap. If your spreadsheet is not updating, check that you are forwarding to the correct Zapier inbox address — each Zap has its own unique address. Find it in the Trigger section of your Zap editor.

**Mistake 2: Mismatched column headers**
If Zapier cannot find a column in your spreadsheet, it will skip that field. Make sure your spreadsheet column headers match exactly what you typed in the mapping screen — a space or a missing word will break the connection. Double-check spelling and capitalisation.

**Mistake 3: Leaving the Zap unpublished**
Many users complete the setup and test it successfully, but forget to click **Publish**. An un-published Zap only runs during testing and stops as soon as you close the editor. Always click Publish when you are ready to use the automation for real.

---

## What this means for you

* **For business owners:** You can eliminate the manual email-to-spreadsheet copying that eats up hours every week. The automation runs in the background, 24 hours a day, so you always have an up-to-date record without lifting a finger.
* **For employees and managers:** Once this first Zap is running, you can build additional automations on top of it — for example, sending a Slack message when a new row appears, or creating a follow-up task in your project tool.
* **If you are just getting started:** Your first Zap does not need to be perfect. Start with one simple task — perhaps forwarding a specific type of inquiry email to your spreadsheet — and expand from there once you see how smoothly it works.
